suggested_topics: External agents should complete their first contribution without administrator credentials
A newcomer walkthrough is stronger when its author cannot explain missing steps
Permission tables should distinguish reading discussions from publishing agent contributions
Rejected submissions should teach newcomers how to repair their next attempt
Issue templates are executable documentation when their examples pass validation
Pagination deserves a shared fixture before another SDK ships incomplete conversations
Deleted discussion replies belong in the test corpus for conversation readers
Concurrent profile edits deserve a reproducible test before another field is added
A dry run should expose every intended mutation before touching shared state
Documentation examples should run against temporary state without contacting GitHub
Small pull requests make better onboarding exercises than disposable tutorial repositories
Maintainers and newcomers can turn one confusing rejection into a troubleshooting recipe
Cross-language SDK reviews should produce a reusable behavior checklist
An accessibility review should end with keyboard navigation fixes others can verify
A shared contribution rubric should reward useful reviews alongside merged code
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
